name: Posterior paratricipital approach to the distal humerus
corridor: Medial and lateral windows around intact triceps insertion with posterior humeral elevation

positioning.text: Position lateral or prone with arm supported, elbow freely flexed, and posterior humerus accessible to fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Review articular comminution and plan dual-column plating, ulnar-nerve handling, and conversion to osteotomy if visualization is inadequate.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark humeral shaft, olecranon, medial/lateral epicondyles, ulnar nerve, and subcutaneous ulna.

incision.text: Use posterior incision from middle-distal humeral junction to ulnar diaphysis, avoiding direct placement over olecranon tip.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps and create an ulnar window after releasing and protecting ulnar nerve to first FCU motor branch.

deep_interval.text: Mobilize triceps from lateral septum and posterior humerus, elevate anconeus posterolaterally, and move intact triceps sleeve medially or laterally for two-window access.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness flaps, medial ulnar-nerve window and lateral triceps-anconeus window, then posterior distal humerus.

structures_encountered.text: Ulnar nerve, triceps, anconeus, medial/lateral columns, posterior capsule, MCL posterior band, and LUCL are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar nerve, radial nerve proximally, anterior MCL band, LUCL, triceps insertion, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Only posterior MCL band and posterolateral capsule may be released for exposure; preserve anterior MCL and LUCL.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid sustained ulnar-nerve traction and excessive displacement of intact triceps sleeve.

exposure.text: Provides medial and lateral column access without triceps detachment or olecranon osteotomy and retains olecranon as reduction template.

limitations.text: Articular visualization is limited for highly comminuted C3 patterns compared with olecranon osteotomy.

extensions.text: Release only posterior capsular bands or convert to olecranon osteotomy when safe direct articular visualization remains inadequate.

indications.text: Use for extra-articular and simple intra-articular distal-humerus fractures, including selected C1-C2 patterns.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer transolecranon or another extensile approach for severe articular comminution requiring complete visualization.

implant_implications.text: Supports orthogonal or parallel dual plating through two windows while preserving triceps insertion; keep ulnar nerve off implants.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and oblique views to verify articular reduction, column alignment, and screw containment where direct view is limited.

closure.text: Repair released capsule, restore anconeus/triceps fascial intervals, and leave ulnar nerve tension free away from sutures and metalwork.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, stiffness, limited articular reduction, nonunion, infection, heterotopic ossification, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: Convert to olecranon osteotomy if direct reduction cannot be verified through the two windows.

procedure_applications.condition: An extra-articular or simple intra-articular distal-humerus fracture can be fixed through triceps-sparing medial and lateral windows

questions.question: Which MCL portion may be released?
questions.answer: The posterior band, while preserving the anterior band.

questions.question: Which lateral ligament must remain intact?
